01 · My story

Eight years of learning to transform what people see

The short version of how a secondary school designer in Nigeria ended up building real-time AI used by 20,000+ people.

In 2018 I spent whole nights breaking one portrait into hundreds of fragments in Photoshop, layer by layer, until it looked like the person was dissolving into the air. In 2026 I build software that turns a streamer into a completely different character, live, for thousands of creators at once. Everything in between is the story of how I got from one to the other.

012018

The kid with Photoshop

I was still a student at Western Boys High School when I opened Photoshop for the first time and gave myself a brand name: Joe Elz Graphix. My first clients were a restaurant that needed a menu flier, a DJ who needed a mixtape cover and a student union planning a party.

Nobody cared that I was young. They cared whether the work made people stop scrolling. That was my first lesson in business: people pay for results they can see, delivered when you said you would deliver them.

022019 – 2025

Learning the machine behind the screen

Design showed me how things should look. I wanted to know how they worked. In 2019 I took a hardware and maintenance course and learned to open up the computers I had been designing on. In 2021 I started Software Engineering at the Federal University of Technology Owerri.

Lectures gave me the theory. I filled the gaps myself, with cybersecurity through Cisco and C# through Microsoft and freeCodeCamp. Somewhere in those years, design and engineering stopped being two separate skills. They became one way of thinking: make it work, then make it feel effortless.

For my final-year project I went deep into AI. I trained a deep learning model that looks at a photo of a tomato leaf and diagnoses which of ten conditions it has, with 99.72% validation accuracy, then wrapped it in a web app a farmer could actually use. It was the first time I taught a machine to see. It wouldn't be the last.

032025

An elite firm for founders who were just starting

In 2025 I founded JayTech Elite Firm. The idea was simple: give young startups the kind of online presence that big companies take for granted. We offered graphic design, web design, branding and cybersecurity under one roof.

Working with founders taught me something no lecture could. Most businesses don't need more tools. They need one product that solves a real problem, built simply enough that anyone can use it. I kept noticing that gap, and I wanted to build into it myself.

04April 2026

Two firsts in one month

In April 2026 I graduated from FUTO with Second Class Upper honours. That same month, I launched SmokeScreen.

The first version was a single HTML file connected to a real-time video AI engine. It let any creator step into a new character live, on an ordinary webcam, with no motion-capture rig, green screen or editing. There was no big launch and no funding. People found it, tried it, and paid for it in the first month.

05Six months later

From one file to a real company

Today SmokeScreen has 20,000+ users and 1,200+ paying customers. That single file became a desktop app, a full web platform, and an Android app now in development. I hired a team across Nigeria and Pakistan, built a creator affiliate program, and led the company through a full payment compliance review.

When our AI engine provider shut our account, we moved to a new one without users noticing. When support messages piled up faster than I could answer, I built an AI agent that replies to customers in my own voice. Every problem became something I could build my way out of.

The thread through all of it is transformation. I used to transform one photo by hand over a whole night. Now I build systems that transform a whole character in real time, for any creator, on any stream.

JayTech has grown with me, from helping startups look good online to helping brands grow with AI. I'm still the designer who wants every pixel to look right. These days, I ship it to production.

02 · Flagship product

SmokeScreen

From a single HTML file to a multi-platform AI company in six months. Click the stages and tabs to see how it was built and grown.

smokescreenapp.com · launched April 2026

Become any character, live. One webcam, no rig.

SmokeScreen is real-time AI character transformation for streamers, content creators and gamers. It reimagines a creator's face, body, style, background and voice as they move and speak, so they can go live as a fantasy hero, an anime persona, a brand mascot or anyone they imagine. What used to take a motion-capture studio and a VFX team now runs on a normal webcam, inside OBS and the streaming tools creators already use.

Live streamingVTubingGamingContent creationCharacter storytellingVirtual events

About 70% of users are new to AI tools, so the product favours plain language, fewer buttons, prompt presets and a guided first run.

0 → 20,000+registered users and 1,200+ paying customers between April and October 2026, revenue-generating from the first month.
Real-time video AINode.jsSupabaseRailwayElectronNext.jsAndroidFlutterwave

  • Every AI capability sits behind an interface. When the original real-time engine account was disabled, the engine moved to a new provider without users noticing.
  • All three apps share one production database, so users keep one account and one credit balance everywhere. New work runs on an isolated staging branch first.
  • Pricing: three one-time activation plans ($20, $75, $120) plus five credit packs, with Voice Changer and Background Changer gated by plan.
  • Creator affiliate program: 15% per referral, with webhooks, anti-fraud logic, a creator dashboard and a monthly leaderboard.
  • Payments: Flutterwave, Paystack, Squad and crypto. Led a two-week processor compliance review to reinstatement.
  • Legal: Terms, a Privacy Policy aligned with the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023, a consent gate and an abuse policy.
  • Offline growth: "SmokeScreen Agents", a paid in-person setup service in Benin, Owerri, Port Harcourt, Abuja, Asaba, Auchi and Ekpoma.
  • Marketing: TikTok Spark Ads, creator partnerships, flash sales, and campaign creative I art-direct.
  • Hired and lead a remote team: a lead developer, a second developer, a brand strategist and support staff across Nigeria and Pakistan.
  • Ran hiring end to end: briefs, screening, interviews, paid trials, probation agreements, NDAs and contracts.
  • Run delivery as approved milestones. The V2 rebuild is nine gated milestones from design system to production QA, with every commit and test logged.
  • Use AI-assisted engineering (Claude Code) daily to audit code, ship fixes and keep a small team moving fast.

● Final-year project · supervised by Dr. Iheanyichukwu Aguwa

Development of a Convolutional Neural Network Model for Tomato Disease Detection

Tomato farmers in Nigeria lose yield and income to diseases that are hard to tell apart by eye. I trained a deep learning model on the PlantVillage dataset that diagnoses a leaf photo as healthy or one of nine diseases, including early blight, late blight, leaf mould and tomato mosaic virus. Farmers upload a photo in a Next.js web app, a FastAPI server runs the model, and the result comes back with a confidence score.
